audioQrFinding.summary: The memory-book renderer implements a REAL per-memory audio/video QR feature ('scan marks'), but the 'sample' book slug's own data has no real share token to encode, so any scan mark it renders is a fabricated placeholder. This is an important correction to MASTER-BRIEF.md's product-boundary table, and a potential future frame-05 asset once verified.
audioQrFinding.howItWorks: book-renderer/src/templates/common/ScanMark.tsx: when the caller has a shareToken (resolved from the manifest's own ManifestMemory.shareToken, minted by the export pipeline for video/audio memories — an owner decision dated 2026-09-14), ScanMark renders an ACTUAL scannable QR encoding shareViewerUrl(shareToken) (book-renderer/src/model/qr.ts) — a real, revocable link. Deliberately takes a TOKEN, never the raw memory id, specifically for revocability (per that file's own header comment). Without a shareToken, it falls back to either a static pre-drawn brand-mark image (no encoded content at all) or, per book-renderer/src/model/fitter.ts:1180, a FABRICATED placeholder short code: 'Fabricates a short, stable placeholder "short code" until phase 2 wires the real momora.co/e/<token> URL.'
audioQrFinding.whyItMatteredHere: store-assets/v2/raw/rejected/book-spread-text-sample.png (page 16 of the sample book) prints a QR-like mark captioned 'listen to it' with the URL momora.co/e/MMAY. Because the sample book's demo data carries no real shareToken, this is the fabricated-placeholder path, not the real-QR path — the printed URL does not necessarily resolve to anything. A non-functional link, and an implication that the PRINTED BOOK itself plays audio, cannot appear in App Store screenshot evidence. This asset was rejected for exactly that reason (see its manifest entry).
audioQrFinding.masterBriefCorrection: MASTER-BRIEF.md's product-boundary table (Audio row) currently bans implying 'a physical book plays audio or contains audio QR codes' as an absolute rule. That rule is factually OUT OF DATE for this codebase: the audio/video QR feature is real and shipped in the renderer (real QR + real revocable token, owner-approved 2026-09-14). The accurate boundary is narrower: a book MAY link back to audio/video via a scan mark IF and only if (a) the underlying memory actually has a minted share token, (b) the momora.co/e/<token> redirect is verified live in production, and (c) the copy is careful to say the book links to the recording online, not that the paper itself plays sound.

thirdPartyIpScreeningCriterion.status: PERMANENT — added 2026-09-20 after a Pikachu shirt and, on a second stricter pass, a Charmander shirt slipped through this task's earlier screening. Apply this criterion to every future book-renderer page-survey, alongside the existing ScanMark/QR check and the placeholder-dimension-art check, from the first pass — do not wait for a coordinator to catch it.
thirdPartyIpScreeningCriterion.criterion: Reject any page where any of the following is visible ANYWHERE in frame, on any sub-photo (not just the largest/first one on the page): (a) a cartoon or licensed character on clothing, toys, bibs, costumes, or backpacks; (b) a visible brand name or logo, including on shoes, packaging/bottles, appliances, storefronts/signage, ride or play equipment, or book covers/spines; (c) sports-team marks; (d) third-party screen content (a TV/tablet/phone showing visible video or app content — off/blank screens are fine). 'Small enough not to notice' is explicitly NOT an exemption (owner directive, 2026-09-20) — if a reviewer can identify it at the render's own native size, it is rejected, and the fact that a compositor will later shrink the image onto a smaller canvas area is not a mitigation, because it can still be identifiable at that reduced scale (verified true for a shirt-sized character graphic in this task).
thirdPartyIpScreeningCriterion.howThisTaskMissedItTheFirstTime: The first pass (before this criterion existed) screened only for ScanMark/QR and placeholder-dimension text, per the ORIGINAL task brief, and judged 'grouping/quality' by looking at the page's most prominent photo. A follow-up coordinator review flagged a Pikachu shirt that WAS on the dominant photo and had simply not been checked for character content. This task then re-screened and picked a new spread (pages 34/35) that looked clean on first inspection — but a SECOND, owner-mandated stricter pass caught a Charmander shirt in that spread's THIRD, smaller sub-photo (the grandmother photo on page 35), which had not been individually zoomed into during the first re-screen. The lesson recorded here for future implementers: inspect EVERY sub-photo on a multi-photo page individually and at real resolution, not just the page's largest/first photo — the violation rate in this particular book (Pokémon-family characters alone appeared on at least 7 of 59 real-photo pages) is high enough that partial screening will miss things.
